[[2013 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] champions |bowl=[[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result=Sweet Sixteen }} {{2012–13 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2012–13 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Miami]] during the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Hurricanes, led by second-year head coach [[Jim Larrañaga]], played their home games at the [[BankUnited Center|Bank United Center]] and were members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. With a veteran roster, the Hurricanes finished the regular season with a conference record of 15–3 and won the ACC regular season championship, marking the program's first-ever outright regular season conference championship. The Hurricanes entered the [[2013 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] as the top-seed and received a first-round bye. After defeating [[2012–13 Boston College Eagles men's basketball team|Boston College]] and [[2012–13 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]], they beat [[2012–13 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] to capture the 2013 ACC tournament championship and became the first ACC school other than [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] or North Carolina to win both the ACC regular season and tournament championships in the same season since the [[1973–74 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|1974 NC State]] team. The Hurricanes were selected as a 2-seed in the South Region of the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2013 NCAA tournament]] and beat 15-seed [[2012–13 Pacific Tigers men's basketball team|Pacific]] in the second round. The Hurricanes beat 7-seed [[2012–13 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] in the third round to advance to the sweet sixteen where they lost to [[2012–13 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]]. They finished the season 29–7, their most victories in a season. They would tie this number of wins ten years later. ==Previous season== The Hurricanes finished the 2011–12 season 20–13 overall, 9–7 in ACC play and lost in the second round of the [[2012 National
